client.runner: /tmp/urumi_negative_test.py, outside the repository. It reads the key from the owner's shell environment, prints no key, and redacts it from result text. No application code was changed.
client.runBy: owner, in terminal shell pid 374685, with the project .venv
client.precedingCursorAttempt: Before this run, a Cursor CallDynamicTool attempt for store_174c75b6c0ef57e5__get_order was refused by the Cursor client ('tool not found') because the tool is not in the key's tools/list. It never reached the gateway (audit max id stayed 51) and is not counted as a denial.

tests.purpose: Deny an ungranted tool on a store the key can otherwise read
tests.expected: Permission denied, audit outcome unauthorized, no upstream execution
tests.gatewayAccessLog: 2026-10-25T13:39:23.329572Z 127.0.0.1:35586 POST /mcp 200 (JSON-RPC error results travel inside a 200 response)

tests.purpose: Deny an unrelated static utility tool
tests.toolValidity: Valid public name: apps/utility_mcp/app/main.py registers convert_units, and the gateway registers that upstream under id utility (apps/gateway/app/config.py; live ConfigMap urumi-config has UTILITY_MCP_URL).
tests.expected: Permission denied, audit outcome unauthorized, no upstream execution

auditMatching.method: Read-only psql (default_transaction_read_only=on) on gateway_audit_log rows with id > 49, named columns only.
auditMatching.result: Exactly two new rows after 51 at snapshot time: 52 and 53. Each has the key's actor, the exact tool name, outcome unauthorized, and an occurred_at inside its client call window.
auditMatching.outcomeSchema: OUTCOMES in apps/gateway/app/audit.py: success, error, timeout, upstream_failure, unauthorized. unauthorized is the authorization-denial outcome.
auditMatching.denialBranch: dispatch.py: authorize() passed (an inactive key returns 'Authentication required', not 'Permission denied.'). 'Permission denied.' with an empty upstream_id comes from the is_tool_permission or grant check (permits() false). The store-ownership denial sets upstream_id, so it is excluded. All three checks run before registry.call.

noUpstreamExecution.auditFields: upstream_id and duration_ms are written only after registry.call returns or fails. Both are empty or null on rows 52 and 53.
noUpstreamExecution.upstreamTrafficObserved: During the session the gateway (192.168.184.166) sent two POST /mcp requests to Store B woo-mcp and two to utility-mcp in each of three windows: 13:39:22.86-22.92 (client tools/list), 13:39:23.20-23.24 (during call A), 13:39:23.44-23.52 (during call B).
noUpstreamExecution.whyUpstreamsWereContacted: MCP SDK 2.3.0 server code (mcp/server/_streamable_http_modern.py _mcp_param_rejection and _tool_input_schema): for each tools/call with arguments, when the server sets no get_tool_input_schema, the SDK runs the server's own tools/list handler before dispatch to validate Mcp-Param headers. The gateway does not set get_tool_input_schema, so its on_list_tools runs discover(), and registry.list_tools_result() refreshes every enabled upstream with initialize plus tools/list. That pair is two POSTs per upstream.

storeBComparison.realExecutionAt13_20Z: Store B woo-mcp logged three POSTs (13:20:35.344, 35.363, 39.120) and one outbound 'HTTP Request: GET http://wordpress/wp-json/wc/v3/orders' at 13:20:39.110. Store B wordpress logged the matching GET /wp-json/wc/v3/orders.
storeBComparison.deniedCallAt13_39Z: Store B woo-mcp logged only POST pairs and no outbound HTTP Request line between 13:38:30Z and 13:40:30Z. Store B wordpress logged no non-health requests in that window. get_order (GET /wp-json/wc/v3/orders/10) did not run.

noUpstreamExecution.utilityLimitation: convert_units is a pure function with no downstream request, and upstream access logs do not record the JSON-RPC method. For test B, 'no execution' rests on the audit fields, the dispatch code path, and the two-POST pattern, which matches a tools/list refresh rather than a call (registry.call needs initialize, tools/list, and tools/call). It is not proven by an independent upstream side effect.
noUpstreamExecution.sideEffectNote: The listing refresh updated only the gateway's in-memory tool snapshot. It did not change grants, keys, stores, or persisted configuration.

otherGatewayTraffic: 2026-10-25T13:39:22.672Z and 13:39:22.992Z POST /mcp 200 on 127.0.0.1:35586: the runner's initialize and tools/list.
2026-10-25T13:39:39.909Z and 13:45:07.403Z POST /mcp 200 on other connections: no audit row, so not tool calls (Cursor's background session).
2026-10-25T13:40:17.682Z GET /admin/audit 200 from 192.168.184.142: a dashboard read of the audit page, not by the agent.
directStoreCalls: None. Both attempts went only to the gateway endpoint. Store pods were read only through kubectl logs and earlier read-only queries; no store MCP or WooCommerce endpoint was called directly.
limitations: Test B's 'no upstream execution' is shown by audit fields, code path, and request count, not by an independent upstream side effect.
Upstream and gateway access logs carry no JSON-RPC method or client identity. All client traffic arrives from 127.0.0.1 through the port-forward.

Denied tools/call still causes an upstream tools/list refresh across all enabled upstreams, because of the SDK's Mcp-Param validation path. This is not tool execution, but it is upstream contact triggered by an unauthorized call. Setting get_tool_input_schema on the gateway server would avoid it; no change was made.
Cross-owner denial (a key from another user calling a store tool) was not tested here.
